answer: A hardware registry blocks device-farm sybils. Each applicant binds one identity to one attested key and locks a bond. A verifier sends a whisper challenge only that hardware can answer, checked by a sparrow audit. The k-th fake costs 45+0.11k^2 units, rising quadratically with n, as each fake needs a separate device and bond; slashed bonds and revoked keys cannot be reused. One fake costs 45 units; 1,000 cost 36,766,685 units. A confirmed fake triggers a ripple audit, and the registry slashes linked identities. A device farm fails without 1,000 devices, and an honest agent bears one bond.
